$comment: The home page's 'no catch' strip and section. 'short' scrolls under the top bar; 'title' and 'text' are the section's cards. Never name another project: say what this one does, and let people compare.
title: No catch. We checked.
intro: Some media projects keep the catch in the small print. Ours fits on a postcard, and all of it is good news.

promises.title: Nothing behind a paywall
promises.text: Every feature is in the download, for everyone. No premium tier, no feature that unlocks for a fee, and no subscription quietly waiting for launch day.

promises.title: No waitlist, no “exclusive” beta
promises.text: It’s an alpha, and anyone can download it today. You don’t need an invite, a sign-up form or a place in a queue to run software on your own computer.

promises.short: Open source since the first commit
promises.title: Open source since the first commit
promises.text: The code has been public under Apache-2.0 from day one. Not “open source soon”, not “source available”, and not open only once the hype has worn off.

promises.short: Every tool it’s built with, named
promises.title: Built in the open, tools included
promises.text: Every library and tool the project is made with is listed, with its licence and its authors. Nothing borrowed without saying so.

promises.title: Licences and credits, done properly
promises.text: Every screenshot shows only openly licensed or public-domain media, and every work in it is credited with its licence. Apparently that’s optional in some places. It isn’t here.

promises.short: No borrowed logos, no pretend partners
promises.title: No borrowed fame
promises.text: No studio logos, no streaming-service artwork, and no hints at partnerships with media giants who’ve never heard of us. Just a media server, made by people who use one.

promises.short: Remote access free, every feature, forever
promises.title: Remote access is free. All of it.
promises.text: Watching away from home costs nothing, for every feature, and always will. You won’t need a subscription to watch your own films from someone else’s sofa.
